Comparison of two runs of acme
  Earlier   read 2026-10-01, scheck 0.0.3, a report file
  Later     read 2026-10-22, scheck 0.0.3, a report file
  20 days between the last reading of the earlier run and the first of the later.

This compares what two runs read. Nothing was contacted and nothing was checked again. It holds the
personal data and internal topology of the reports it compares, for the operator only.

What these two runs can be compared on
  - The engagement file changed between the runs. A finding whose rule reads a declaration from it
    is not confirmed as fixed or new.

Summary
  The earlier run had 10 open findings and 1 accepted (the list below covers both). Since then:
    - 3 fixed
    - 3 still open
    - 1 accepted since
    - 1 no longer reported but not confirmed fixed
    - 2 not checked again
  Not in that count: 1 new, 1 reported for the first time, 1 open again. New means the earlier run
  read it completely and did not find it; reported for the first time means the earlier run had not
  looked.
  1 moved to another asset and 1 renamed; they are counted once, where they stand now.

New since the earlier run
  - [high] The kernel is past its end of support on deploy. The earlier run read it completely and
    did not find it.

Reported for the first time
  - [medium] SSH allows root to sign in on db1. The earlier run did not include this asset.

Open again
  - [high] A sensitive service listens without a firewall on web (6379/tcp). It was accepted before;
    the acceptance by carol ran out (until 2026-10-10), so it is on the list again.

Fixed
  - A credential is in the repository's history on api (aws:AKIA@9f8e7d6c5b4a) (rated high before).
    The check ran in full on 2026-10-22 and did not find it. Removing a credential from the code
    does not show it was changed: whether it was revoked or rotated was not checked, and anyone who
    copied it could still use it.
  - The firewall allows inbound traffic by default on web (rated medium before). The check ran in
    full on 2026-10-22 and did not find it.
  Also 1 at low severity or informational; see -v.

Still open
  - [high] A Workspace account has no 2-step verification on workspace (alice.smith@example.com)
    (renamed from alice@example.com).
  - [high] SSH accepts passwords on deploy (moved from deploy (host:203.0.113.5:22); the same
    machine id, so scheck takes it for the same machine).
  Also 1 at low severity or informational; see -v.

Accepted since the earlier run, not fixed
  - [medium] SSH allows many authentication attempts on web. dave agreed to live with it (until
    2027-01-31); the reason given: decided.

No longer reported, not confirmed fixed
  The later check did not report these, but something that has to hold before scheck calls a finding
  fixed did not hold. Check them by hand, or compare two runs made with the same scheck release, the
  same file and the same access.
  You changed the engagement file, and the rule reads declarations from it:
    - [high] A Workspace account has no 2-step verification on workspace (bob@example.com)

Not checked again
  The later run did not look at these, so nothing is said about them either way. Not looking is not
  a fix.
  The asset is not in the later run; removing it from scope does not fix it, and if it was shut down
  scheck did not check that:
    - [medium] SSH allows root to sign in on db1
  The asset was not read this time: the access scheck was given cannot read this; it needs contents,
  read-only where the provider offers it:
    - [high] A credential is in the repository's history on shop (aws:AKIA@0a1b2c3d4e5f)

Assets that changed
  - db1 (host:203.0.113.20:22) is no longer in the engagement. Removing it from scope does not fix
    anything on it.
  - deploy moved from host:203.0.113.5:22 to host:203.0.113.9:22, the same machine or tenant.
  - shop was collected and is now failed. The access scheck was given cannot read this; it needs
    contents, read-only where the provider offers it.
  - db1 was added to the engagement (host:203.0.113.22:22).

Exit 1: attention needed. 3 new, first-reported, open-again or raised findings at or above the
threshold. Exit 1 here counts what got worse. Findings that are still open in the later run (5 at or
above the threshold) are not what it counts.
